svg.title: macOS · Guided clip (experimental) · canvas & opening step, tall output · 1000×700
svg.desc: Mirrors App/GuidedBuilderView.swift (railLayout · rail · canvasStep · openingControls · framingStage · flowStrip) and App/GuidedCanvasFrame.swift — the guided builder's first step on a wide surface, as reworked after the 2026-08-12 mac UI review ("layout is yuk", "wasted space", "no overview"). From 700pt wide and 500pt tall the flow swaps the paged survey for a STEPS RAIL; below that it keeps the iOS column. The rail is 252pt: "Guided clip" with the EXPERIMENTAL capsule beside it, one numbered row per step (done = accent disc + checkmark, current = accent ring on an accent-10% row, todo = grey disc), ANSWERS WRITTEN BACK as subtitles, completed rows clickable, "Open in the full editor" at the foot. The CONTENT COLUMN caps at 1160pt and centres in the pane, so a 32-inch display gets a composed page instead of controls pinned against the rail; the stage scales with window height (340pt at the 700-tall window drawn here, up to 620pt on a tall display). ONE STAGE FOR EVERY STEP, always with a picture: while the opening's framing is Wide the stage is the OUTPUT ITSELF — GuidedCanvasFrame draws the exact decoded first frame at the chosen shape (badge "Frame 1 — exact · as shot"; a cropping shape reads e.g. "· 2160×1214" from VideoCanvasCropper.cropSize and gains the drag + amber source strip, offset → AppModel.blendCanvasOffset) — and a punched opening swaps the same stage to the GuidedFramingBox with its target/curve chips and the role caption "The clip opens in this framing — punched in from the very first frame." (the answer to "does it start wide then end on the rectangle?" — it doesn't; the punch is there from frame one). Never two pictures pretending to be a before-and-after. The shape is a pop-up menu on the question row; options carry their cropSize consequence plus "Recentre crop" once the crop is off centre. Chips follow the one idiom everywhere: selected = white on accent, unselected = white card pill (the old black-on-accent and secondary-grey fills died in this review); the active speed chip keeps LL.ink + amber. THE OVERVIEW STRIP sits above the bottom bar on every step: one block per stretch, width proportional to the output seconds it contributes (compiled stretchFrames), base runs as white cards, moments as LL.ink with the amber speed label, a viewfinder glyph on punched stretches, "cut"/"1s" seam connectors from the COMPILED ease, the stretch being answered outlined in accent, the exact total at the trailing end; answered blocks are clickable (same reachability rule as the rail — no dimmed disabled look). Back/Next are push buttons bottom-trailing, Next = accent + .defaultAction; on step one, Back returns to the PROJECT the flow was opened from (model.finishFlow(openProject:true) → the project detail page), not the Create home. NEW 2026-08-12 (same-day follow-up): the OUTPUT RATE menu sits above OPENING — every duration in the flow is output seconds at this rate and it gates how deep slow motion goes, so it cannot hide until Review (it stays there too); the rail writes it back into the canvas row ("9:16 · 50 fps · 100× streaks"). On macOS the shape and rate menus render BORDERLESS (accent label + up/down chevrons — AppKit ignores the label chip); iOS draws the white chip. The floating pill tab bar overlays the window bottom centre with NO TAB HIGHLIGHTED while the guided flow fronts the Create tab (FloatingTabBar showsSelection:false — highlighting Create would claim its home screen is showing); it is not drawn here to keep the strip legible. Verified 2026-08-12 on the Mac at 1660×1183 and the 760×680 default (which stacks the two columns), and on the iPad Pro 11/13 sims. NEW 2026-08-12 (scrub preview): the stage is wrapped in GuidedScrubOverlay (App/GuidedScrubPreview.swift) and under the pane, 8pt below and exactly its width, sits the GuidedScrubStrip — a 22pt white-card capsule covering this step's slice of the finished clip's clock (GuidedScrubContext.window(forStretch:0) — stretch 1 plus its compiled trailing ease; the seam here is a cut, so 0s…2.3s on this file's 50 fps sample data — the sim run behind the screenshots was 25 fps and read 3.5s). Idle the strip shows the window start/end as 9pt semibold secondary labels inside both ends and a centred accent eye + "Preview" (10pt semibold) — the strip sits above the caption line, which moved down to make room. DESC-ONLY STATES, not drawn: (1) scrub-active — GuidedScrubDisplay replaces the pane's picture with the ≈ preview at the scrubbed moment, bottom-leading black-55% capsule badge "≈ preview · 1.2s of 21s" (white bold 10pt), while a 14pt accent knob with a 1.5pt white ring rides the bar; (2) drag-locked — a finished drag holds the preview and an ✕ (xmark.circle.fill, secondary) appears trailing OUTSIDE the bar to let it go; (3) macOS hover-to-peek — hovering the STRIP scrubs and clears on exit unless locked. The canvas pane itself does NOT hover- or drag-scrub (allowsPaneScrub:false on this step): it composes the crop, so its drag keeps moving the frame and the scrub lives on the strip alone.

g.text: What shape should the clip be?
The shape sits above everything it changes — every framing below is composed against it.
Every duration below counts in seconds at this rate — and it
sets how deep slow motion can go.
Usually this stays wide — the punch belongs to the moment.
This is the output — the clip keeps the shape it
